title: Ephemeral Admin Sandbox and Task Replayability for Support Automation
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem: Oncall and Support engineers need to run short-lived admin utilities (DB queries, cache invalidations, model-route toggles) during incidents and standard ops flows. Today we rely on ad-hoc scripts and long-lived admin shells which leak context, cause noisy logs, and are hard to replay for postmortem/debugging. There is also risk of accidental secrets exposure when helpers run in non-sanitized environments.

Goal: Build an "ephemeral admin sandbox" that executes admin utilities as first-class tasks (runbooks-as-tasks) with: short-lived scoped credentials, step-level telemetry and deterministic replay tokens, automated input/output sanitization, policy gates for risky actions, and an audit trail suitable for compliance. The sandbox should integrate with the existing task-runner API and the ops console (trace view + step re-run).

Scope and deliverables (MVP):
- A lightweight sandbox wrapper library (go/python) that: provisions ephemeral creds (minimally scoped), injects a telemetry context (trace id + replay token), and enforces input/output sanitizers.
- Task metadata schema additions: step_type, risk_level, required_approval, replayable:true/false, sanitizer_profile.
- Console UI hooks: show ephemeral task trace, mark steps replayable, and surface replay tokens to authorized users only.
- CLI helper for support engineers to run tasks locally but execute against sandboxed runner in the cluster (no local secrets leaked).
- Audit log format extension capturing sanitized inputs, ephemeral credential id, and replay token mapping.

Non-goals (MVP): automatic rollback orchestration, long-running batch transformations, replacing heavy orchestration engines.

Design notes and trade-offs: 
- Ephemeral creds: use short-lived KMS-backed service tokens issued by an internal credential broker. Trade-off: token issuance has latency (~150-300ms) which we accept for better security; we will implement client-side warm pools for common tasks if needed.
- Replay model: replay tokens point to a frozen snapshot of inputs and a pointer to a task image (immutable). Replaying will not re-issue external side-effecting credentials automatically; replay runs are executed under a "replay sandbox" with an enforced dry-run unless an explicit supervisor approval is present. This trades convenience for safety.
- Sanitization: implement a hook-based sanitizer pipeline (regex + allowlist) configurable by sanitizer_profile. Edge cases (binary blobs, proprietary model weights) will be rejected unless a special bypass is approved.
- Performance: wrapper adds ~5–15ms overhead per step plus credential latency. Acceptable for interactive ops flows.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Support engineer can run a guarded admin task via CLI that provisions ephemeral creds and completes end-to-end in the sandbox in a test org.
2) Trace in Console shows step-by-step telemetry and a replay token for every run that opted into replayable:true.
3) Audit logs capture sanitized input/outputs, ephemeral_cred_id, and a PR link for the task implementation.
4) Security team can run a red-team scenario (scripted) demonstrating that ephemeral tokens have limited scope and expire as expected.
5) Unit and integration tests for sanitizer profiles with >= 90% coverage for common sanitizer rules.

Risks and mitigation:
- Accidental exposure of sensitive outputs: mitigation via default-deny sanitizer and an escalation path for overrides.
- Developers bypassing sandbox for convenience: mitigation via CI policy that flags long-lived credential usage in new PRs and training.
- Replay causing unsafe side effects: mitigate by defaulting replays to dry-run and requiring two-person approval to execute replays that alter state.

Longer-term: coordinate with "task graph" initiative to support checkpointed retries, automatic rollback step templates, and richer role-based replay permissions.
acceptance_criteria:
1) CLI-run admin task completes with ephemeral creds in test org and returns trace ID.
2) Console displays trace, step timings, and a replay token when task metadata has replayable:true.
3) Audit logs include sanitized_inputs, sanitized_outputs, ephemeral_cred_id, and task implementation PR URL.
4) Security sign-off on ephemeral token lifecycle and sanitizer profile.
5) Integration tests exercising sanitizer profiles and replay dry-run behavior.
